This event occurred in November, a shoulder month, when a significant amount of maintenance is performed on BES lines and equipment.

SPP identified in its Real-time Assessment (RTA)13 studies that the simultaneous outages of the Aeolus–Clover line and the Miracle Mile West main bus would require mitigation plans to maintain the reliable operation of the BES.
SPP informed WACM that there was not a good mitigation plan to support overlapping the outage of their Miracle Mile West main bus and PACE Aeolus–Clover 500 kV line.
RCW also indicated that if WACM would like to proceed with its Miracle Mile West main bus outage, PACE agreed to limit its wind as needed to mitigate any overloads.

Their study identified that about 400 MW of wind reduction would be needed to mitigate the loading on the Alcova–Miracle Mile East line. WACM studies showed that if the Aeolus–Clover line was removed from service, the loading would increase to over 130% with the next contingent loss of the Dave Johnston–Goshen 230 kV line, even with the 400 MW of previously identified wind reductions. SPP informed RCW of significant reliability concerns on the WACM Alcova–Miracle Mile East line loading if overlapped with the PACE outage, and use of area phase-shifters would not be enough to mitigate the exceedances. Studies conducted by SPP, RCW, and WACM all indicated the need for additional reductions to PACE wind generation in the area. The RCs discussed relaying this information to PACE to determine whether it would begin reducing wind generation before the planned 500 kV line outage.

The high-level takeaways that should be considered by all stakeholders and acted upon accordingly include the following: • Poor Solar PV Data Resolution: Almost all solar PV facilities involved in this disturbance were not able to provide adequate information to the analysis team to fully understand the causes of tripping and develop recommended mitigating actions.

Updates to reporting these types of events (not necessarily with quick turnaround times) will help industry improve their situational awareness of abnormal inverter-based resource performance and possible issues needing mitigating action by facility owners to improve their performance. • Inverter Tripping: There were three causes of BPS-connected solar PV tripping during this disturbance—ac overcurrent protection, dc low voltage protection, and ac low voltage protection.
